answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it earns reputation: think of copper wiring that only real operators lay, while fake identities crumble like shale under load. Reputation should accrue slowly through attested work, not purchased in bulk, and sinkholes in the trust graph - karst-like gaps where fake clusters hide - can be exposed by cross-checking independent attestations, so cheap copies cannot blend into the productive economy.
